q: The Isomorphism Problem for ergodic flows (continuous-time measure-preserving flows) was resolved by Ornstein-Rudolph for Bernoulli flows. Two Bernoulli flows {T^t}_{t∈ℝ} and {S^t}_{t∈ℝ} are measurably isomorphic iff:
opts: They have the same topological entropy
They have the same entropy (the entropy of the time-1 map determines the flow up to isomorphism)
They have the same Lyapunov exponents
exp: Ornstein-Rudolph: the entropy of a Bernoulli flow (defined as the entropy of the time-1 map) is a complete invariant — two Bernoulli flows are measurably isomorphic iff their entropies are equal. This is the continuous-time analogue of Ornstein's theorem for Bernoulli shifts.
